newsitem.title: USA: First Interregional Advisors Corp sued by SEC.
newsitem.headline: First Interregional Advisors Corp sued by SEC.

text.p: - A bankrupt brokerage was accused in a federal lawsuit Friday of defrauding 1,700 investors who put an estimated $50 million into its packaged government leases.

The suit, filed by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, said First Interregional Advisors Corp of Milburn had sold the income from leases to investors, in much the same way that other firms bundle and sell mortgage income. But, the lawsuit charges, the brokerage sold the same lease assignments to as many as three investors.
The packages were ostensibly backed by leases of equipment taken by government agencies.
The federal watchdog said revenues to early investors came from later investments. The typical investment was $44,000, said Andrew Geist, associate regional director for the SEC's New York office.

The company filed for Chapter 11 protection on Wednesday, and U.S. District Judge Maryanne Trump Barry on Thursday froze the assets of the brokerage and its president, Richard Goettlich of Mendham. It shares offices and staff with First Interregional Equity Corp.
